summary.text: Rick Pressnell is the Democratic candidate for Alabama House of Representatives District 2 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Ben Harrison (R).

A retired Huntsville police supervisor and Army National Guard colonel, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that his priorities include Medicaid expansion, a state lottery for education and protecting the environment.

paragraphs.text: Rick Pressnell graduated from Clements High School, earned a graduate degree from Auburn University at Montgomery in 1999, and earned a graduate degree from the U.S. Army War College in 2013.
He served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1976 to 1980.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Pressnell said he was born and raised in Limestone County, has been married for 35 years, and spent 21 years as a Huntsville police officer and supervisor.
He said he is a retired Army colonel from the Alabama Army National Guard and a combat veteran with two master's degrees.
The Democratic primary for District 2 was canceled, and Pressnell advanced to the general election without appearing on a primary ballot.

Pressnell said he wrote Alabama's law on providing a false name to a law enforcement officer, which Rep. Randy Hinshaw introduced, and he named public safety and community policing as policy interests.
He also said he is a longtime member of the Tennessee Riverkeepers and a certified master naturalist, and he listed VoteVets among his endorsers.
